newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian police arrest third Albanian "terrorist".
newsitem.headline: Serbian police arrest third Albanian "terrorist".

text.p: Serbian police on Monday arrested a member of an Albanian "terrorist group" responsible for bomb attacks in the mainly Albanian-populated province of Kosovo, Yugoslav news agency Tanjug reported.
It said Idriz Haljiti Aslani from Vuciturn had taken part in two bomb attacks on a police station and a refugee camp in Vuciturn.
The interior ministry was continuing to search for the other members of the group, it said.
Serbian police arrested two local Albanians on terrorism charges last week.
They said Besim Rama from the village of Prekaze and Avni Nura from Prelovac belonged to a group that killed three policeman and a civilian and wounded seven police in attacks from 1993 to mid-1996.

Kosovo's 90 percent ethnic Albanian majority has boycotted Serbian authority since Belgrade clamped down on the province in 1989, stripping it of autonomy and claiming the Albanians wanted to secede from Serbia.
The Democratic League of Kosovo (DLK), which represents the interests of Kosovo Albanians, accuses Serbia of systematic human rights abuses.
There have been a series of attacks on Serbian police this year but few suspects were arrested and police displayed unusual restraint.
In a landmark deal last month, Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic and DLK leader Ibrahim Rugova agreed on the return of Albanian students to official schools after a six-year boycott.
Police who arrested the two suspects found weapons used in the crimes and a large quantity of other firearms, ammunition and explosives, the interior ministry said.
